cycle_78.the_hypothesis: hcli/tool_registry.py's _shell_readonly still admits `sed` into its read-only allowlist -- or, if that set was pruned, its two guards (the forbidden-option set and the path-containment check) both miss a `sed` script whose `w` flag writes a file from INSIDE the script argument, so a registry holding only READ_ONLY can write through shell.readonly.
cycle_78.why_this_is_a_good_hypothesis: it is falsifiable, it names a file and a function, it names its own discriminator (hcli/tests/test_readonly_shell_cannot_write.py), it is disjunctive in a way that survives either state of the allowlist, and it is a real privilege-escalation SHAPE rather than a cosmetic defect -- a read-only guard that can be talked into writing is exactly the class the campaign's own governance lesson is about (protect every path that can WEAKEN a check, not just the one that performs it).
